answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but a claim earns payment only after a randomly selected peer with a stake bond verifies it against a signed, publicly auditable task receipt. A false claim burns the verifier’s bond and excludes both parties from the next epoch; honest peers can appeal with another receipt, letting a ripple of scrutiny expose collusion. The copper bond must exceed the likely payout, so an attacker needs many funded identities and risks losing capital on each fabricated claim; a willow-thin identity alone earns nothing.
